exact_statement: For every finite indexed family of nonempty physical supports, put t_j=2^(-width_j), rho=sum_j t_j and give each local subset law mass1-t_j to empty and t_j^2/(1-t_j) to each particular nonempty mask. Choose an actual anchor j with prior t_j/rho, force its local mask uniform nonempty and draw all other local masks independently in fixed order. The full physical-union output law is Q(A)=rho^(-1)sum_(z:union z=A)K(z)mu(z), normalized on nonempty physical sets; its optimal posterior is over the distinct actual pairs(anchor,local-mask-tuple), including allocation ambiguity. An exact two-array union/occupation dynamic program computes Q in O(2^n sum_j 2^width_j) rational operations. If the supports cover all relevant coordinates Q has full nonempty support. In particular for every finite nonempty list of positive clause widths w_j, U the product of disjoint OR clauses on those widths and F=2U(X)[1-U(-Y)]-1 on independent clones, the same anchor construction on both physical clause copies has complete nonempty actual-posterior cost C_Q(F)<155I(F)/24<7I(F). This is a new clause-mask reference, not an original-prime queue or a canonical partition-forest claim.
hypotheses: Uniform independent physical cube for the Boolean cost theorem; entropy and cost in bits.
Local support instances, the anchor draw and the canonical subsequent local mask draws are actual random choices; aliases or shuffled descriptions of one draw tuple are not counted as distinct runs.

The general pushforward normalizes for overlap, but its <7I payment requires the stated disjoint paired-clause Boolean family. No universal influence payment on arbitrary overlapping supports is asserted.
The new reference has its own explicit priors and local probabilities and is not claimed to be a mixture or subfamily of the original prime queues.
proof_source: SHARED_TAG.md sections1--5, including equation(2a) and the exact union/occupation recursion

exact_statement: For any finite relevant-coordinate support cover and any nonconstant Boolean function, fixed rational allocation witnesses give the complete nonempty uniform-mask pushforward cost upper bound C_e(Q_alpha)<=B(alpha)+v ln Z<=B(alpha) in DUAL.md. Minimizing B over all physical-coordinate incidence constraints is convex. The coordinate-price dual in equation (2) is valid, and rational feasible activations and nonnegative prices satisfying equation (3) certify a global optimum of this fixed-witness bound by exact arithmetic. This does not assert convexity or global optimality of the true pushforward cost, nor universal influence payment.
hypotheses: Activation probabilities lie strictly between zero and one; all sums of incident activation probabilities are at most one.
Witnesses are fixed distributions on actual mask tuples with physical union equal to each nonempty spectral output; all local subset draws and the global nonempty normalization are paid.
Natural logarithms in the optimization; divide by ln 2 for bits.

exact_statement: For every integer w>=8, set r=w*2^w and f=2[z OR product_(j=1)^r OR_w(X_j)]-1 on one common physical bit and disjoint private blocks. Every whole-set reference that chooses any nonempty active-support set among E_j={z} union X_j and then independently samples uniform nonempty local subsets, and every mixture of such references, has C_Q(f)/I(f)>w/4, while H(f)/I(f)<35/8. This includes every globally incidence-feasible independent activation vector and every retuning or mixture of forced-anchor activation samplers on these same uniform dictionaries.
hypotheses: Uniform physical cube; entropy and complete nonempty code cost in bits; physical flip influence.

Active supports are chosen before their independent uniform nonempty subset draws; dictionaries remain the specified supports. Adding a core atom or changing local subset laws is outside the refuted class.
Zero reference probability at a positive spectral atom is interpreted as infinite cost.
